page.intro: The percentages you see here are <bold>historical frequency</bold>, not a promise of what will happen: they count how often something happened before, always alongside the number of matches used. That's not the same as a guaranteed probability. <link>More on how to read them →</link>

winProb.highConfidenceTip: Double chance at 80% or more. In {{seasons}} it was right ~{{low}} of the time between 80% and 85%, and ~{{high}} from 85%.
winProb.highConfidenceCoverage: It applies to ~{{min}}–{{max}} of matches; they are usually clear favourites.
winProb.historyRef: Reference: always choosing 1X would have been right {{pct}} of the time. The best double chance is never estimated below 66.7% (it only leaves out the least likely result).
winProb.calibrationIntro: Each match contributes its three probabilities (home, draw and away). Each band compares the average announced probability with what happened.
winProb.note: Statistical estimate using data from before the match; the market tends to be slightly more accurate. This is not betting advice.

predictor.intro: What to expect from each team based on their earlier league matches (this season and last): what they usually do and what the opponent usually concedes, allowing for home and away and with more weight on recent games. For yellow cards, the referee too. It's an estimate, not what will happen.
predictor.caption: Expected stats for {{home}} and {{away}}
predictor.errorTitle: Average error per team when the predictor was tested on matches already played
predictor.sample: Based on {{home}} home matches of {{homeTeam}} and {{away}} away matches of {{awayTeam}}.
predictor.sampleAll: Based on {{home}} matches of {{homeTeam}} and {{away}} of {{awayTeam}} (home and away), this season and last.
predictor.lowSample: With so few matches, the estimate stays close to the league average.
predictor.refereeBase: Yellow cards with referee {{name}}: {{matches}} of their league matches, this season and last.
predictor.needsReferee: Yellow cards are only estimated once a referee is appointed: without one, they don't beat the league average.
predictor.errorNote: ±: average error per team when tested on the {{matches}} matches of {{from}} and {{to}}, each one using only earlier matches. It has between {{min}} and {{max}} less error than the league average.
predictor.excluded: No estimate: {{stats}}. In that test they didn't have less error than both the league and the team average.
predictor.excludedReferee: They don't improve either when the appointed referee is taken into account.
predictor.notReal: The model's estimate before the match, not real data. Once it is played, you will see the real figures here compared with this prediction.
